questions.q: Tell me about a job or situation where you spoke in English with customers or colleagues every day. What kind of conversations were they?
questions.looks_for: Speaks in full sentences about a real setting, gives examples of conversations (queries, explanations, updates), and sounds comfortable and clear.

questions.q: Describe a time you had to explain something in English to someone who did not understand at first. How did you make it clear?
questions.looks_for: Specific case; used simpler words, slowed down, gave an example or repeated in steps, checked understanding; shows patience.

questions.q: What makes someone easy to understand on a phone call, apart from grammar?
questions.looks_for: Speed, clear pronunciation, pauses, simple words, polite tone, confirming understanding; shows awareness that the customer cannot see them.

questions.q: How do you politely say no to a customer in English when you cannot do what they ask?
questions.looks_for: Gives a polite phrase, apologises without blaming, explains the reason simply, and offers an alternative or next step.

questions.q: If you do not understand a customer's accent or a word they said, what should you do?
questions.looks_for: Politely asks them to repeat or spell, repeats back to confirm, never guesses or pretends; stays respectful of the accent.

questions.q: A customer is speaking very fast and sounds upset about a wrong bill. In English, what would you say to them in the first minute?
questions.looks_for: Calm, polite opening in good English: greets, apologises for the trouble, asks for details, repeats the issue, promises to check; clear and natural speech.

questions.q: Why do you want this English customer support job, when can you join (state your notice period), and what monthly salary do you expect?
questions.looks_for: Clear reason linked to the work, states notice period or joining date in days or weeks, and gives an expected monthly or yearly salary figure or range without dodging.
